---
title: Layout
description: Boxes, rows and columns, filling space, layering and scrolling
---

Every element is a box. Layout is Flutter's, with nothing added: a parent hands its child constraints (the least and most it may be), the child picks a size within them, and the parent places it. There is no CSS.

```tsx
import { Text, View } from "solid-fuse";

<View padding={16} layout={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Text fontSize={18}>Title</Text>
  <Text>Body</Text>
</View>
```

## Rows and columns

Several children are a column. `layout` on the parent says otherwise: a row, a gap, how they align. Every element with children takes it, generated widgets with a single `child` too (`Card`, `Padding`, `DecoratedBox`...), so you rarely need Flutter's `Row` and `Column`. A `<Modal>` among the children takes no part in the layout.

```tsx
{/* Horizontal row with spacing */}
<View layout={{ direction: "horizontal", gap: 12 }}>
  <Text>Left</Text>
  <Text>Right</Text>
</View>

{/* Centered content filling available space */}
<View layout={{ align: "center", justify: "center", expand: true }}>
  <Text>Centered</Text>
</View>

{/* Space between items */}
<View layout={{ justify: "spaceBetween" }}>
  <Text>Start</Text>
  <Text>End</Text>
</View>
```

### layout

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `string` | `"vertical"` | `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"` |
| `gap` | `number` | `0` | Spacing between children (pixels) |
| `align` | `string` | `"start"` | Cross-axis: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, `"stretch"` |
| `justify` | `string` | `"start"` | Main-axis: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"`, `"spaceEvenly"` |
| `expand` | `boolean` | `false` | Fill available space on main axis |

## Filling the width

Layout follows Flutter: a child of a column takes its own width, not the column's. To make one child fill the cross axis, give it `width={Infinity}` (Flutter's `double.infinity`). To make every child fill it, use `align: "stretch"`; as in Flutter, that overrides the children's own widths.

```tsx
<View layout={{ gap: 12 }}>
  <View width={64} height={64} decoration={{ shape: "circle", color: "#F97316" }} />
  <View width={Infinity} height={48} decoration={{ color: "#F97316", borderRadius: 12 }} />
  <View width={Infinity}>
    <Text textAlign="center">Centered in the full width</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## flex

`flex` on a child gives it a share of the free space along the layout's main axis, as CSS `flex: 1` and Flutter's `Expanded(flex: 1)` do. Every element takes it, generated widgets too (`<Card flex={1}>`); it means something only inside a layout (an element with several children, a `Row`, a `Column`).

```tsx
<View layout={{ direction: "horizontal", expand: true }}>
  <View flex={1} decoration={{ color: "#EF4444" }}>
    <Text>Takes remaining space</Text>
  </View>
  <View width={100} decoration={{ color: "#2563EB" }}>
    <Text>Fixed 100px</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Sizes

`width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` and `aspectRatio` on a `View` size the box. `Infinity` means "as large as the parent allows". `margin` is space outside the box, `padding` inside. `alignment` places a single child within a box larger than it.

```tsx
<View width={Infinity} height={200} alignment="center">
  <Text>In the middle</Text>
</View>
```

## Layering

`Stack` layers children on top of each other. `Positioned` places children at specific coordinates within the stack.

```tsx
import { Positioned, Stack, Text, View } from "solid-fuse";

<Stack alignment="center">
  <View width={200} height={200} decoration={{ color: "#2563EB" }} />
  <Positioned top={10} right={10}>
    <Text color="#FFFFFF">Badge</Text>
  </Positioned>
</Stack>
```

| Stack prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alignment` | `AlignmentGeometry` | Default alignment for children |
| `fit` | `string` | `"loose"`, `"expand"`, `"passthrough"` |
| `clipBehavior` | `string` | Clip overflowing children |

| Positioned prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `top` / `left` / `right` / `bottom` | `number` | Offset from stack edges |
| `width` / `height` | `number` | Fixed dimensions |

## Scrolling

A box doesn't scroll. Put content that may not fit in a `ScrollView`:

```tsx
import { ScrollView, Text, View } from "solid-fuse";

<ScrollView padding={16}>
  <View layout={{ gap: 8 }}>
    <For each={items()}>{(item) => <Text>{item}</Text>}</For>
  </View>
</ScrollView>
```

For long lists, see [Lists and scrolling](/docs/build/lists).

## Not like CSS

| You expect | What happens | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| A column child is as wide as the column | It is as wide as its content | `width={Infinity}` on the child, or `align: "stretch"` on the parent |
| A box with `flex={1}` fills the screen | `flex` only means something inside a layout that has a size | Give the parent a size (`height={Infinity}`, or `flex` in its own parent) |
| Content that doesn't fit scrolls | It overflows, with a striped warning in debug | Wrap it in a `ScrollView` |
| A `ScrollView` in a column scrolls | It grows as tall as its content and overflows the column | Give it `flex={1}` |
| `margin: auto` centres | There is no auto margin | `layout={{ align: "center", justify: "center" }}` on the parent, or `alignment="center"` |

Flutter's own guide, [Understanding constraints](https://docs.flutter.dev/ui/layout/constraints), applies as written.
